_doctrine: THE COMMONS LEDGER's source taxonomy (the fourth question: whose knowledge is this pressed from — and does the walk return it, or enclose it?). Each entry names a source the curriculum's artifacts are pressed from, its KIND, and what was taken. KINDS: named_thinker (a person the record kept), artisan_tradition (collective craft whose members the record mostly dropped), craft_labor (working knowledge, often gendered/unwaged, rarely credited), folk_code (anonymous programmer culture), nature_computes (organisms/matter as the original algorithm — credited to be honest about where 'our' mathematics was found). Patterns are case-insensitive regex matched against artifact text (registry description + @identity + voltage). Authored, extendable — add sources as the book's attributions grow.

sources.name: The Alhambra's artisans
sources.pressed: the seventeen wallpaper groups, completed in tile centuries before group theory counted them

sources.name: Pompeii's mosaicists
sources.pressed: tiling algorithms run in stone — meander, opus sectile, guilloche — two millennia before the word 'algorithm'

sources.name: Weavers and textile workers
sources.pressed: the addressable grid, the loom's threading/tie-up/treadling — the first stored program, mostly women's unwaged or underpaid labor

sources.name: Masons and builders
sources.pressed: glide symmetry in brick bond, load paths, the arch — structural knowledge held in hands and rules of thumb

sources.name: The 10 PRINT folk-coders
sources.pressed: one-line generative culture — maze-making as shared idiom, author unknown, endlessly retyped

sources.name: RAND's human computers
sources.pressed: a million random digits (1955) — chance manufactured by rooms of mostly-uncredited staff

sources.name: Euclid
sources.pressed: construction order — nothing before what it is built from; the postulates as ground

sources.name: The Pythagorean school
sources.pressed: whole-number proportion, the triangle's rigidity — and the crisis of the irrational they tried to drown

sources.name: Zeno of Elea
sources.pressed: the paradox of the infinitely divisible — the portal the curriculum walks through

sources.name: Fibonacci (and Indian mathematicians before him)
sources.pressed: the recurrence — carried from Indian arithmetic into Europe; the golden thread

sources.name: Albrecht Dürer
sources.pressed: Melencolia's polyhedron — geometry carrying grief; completion as mourning

sources.name: Lucio Fontana
sources.pressed: the cut — the primitive as violence to the plane; individuation's cost

sources.name: Paul Klee
sources.pressed: the line as a walk — drawing as time, trace as biography

sources.name: Le Corbusier
sources.pressed: the Modulor — measure normalized to one body and imposed on all others

sources.name: Josef Albers
sources.pressed: colour as relation — the same swatch changed by its neighbours, forty years of proof

sources.name: Piet Mondrian
sources.pressed: De Stijl's legislation — primaries and orthogonals as ideology

sources.name: Wassily Kandinsky
sources.pressed: the Bauhaus triad — synesthetic correspondence decreed

sources.name: Mark Rothko

sources.name: The Bauhaus
sources.pressed: discipline as palette — craft pedagogy industrialized

sources.name: The Memphis Group
sources.pressed: refusal as palette — the same geometry, opposed politics

sources.name: Jackson Pollock
sources.pressed: action painting — randomness given a body and a floor

sources.name: Gian Lorenzo Bernini
sources.pressed: the baroque marble that noise dissolves — the classical as the thing procedurality answers

sources.name: Alexander Calder
sources.pressed: the balanced mobile — equilibrium as sculpture, the lever law hung in air

sources.name: Antoni Gaudí
sources.pressed: form-finding by hung chain — gravity as co-designer, the inverted catenary

sources.name: Frei Otto
sources.pressed: soap-film roofs — minimal surfaces found, not drawn

sources.name: M. C. Escher

sources.name: D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson
